title: Smaller Than It Used to Be

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager finds the rock pool of their childhood is tiny: jump off the giant rock anyway, or sit and remember.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has wandered down to the rock pool where (subject.he/she) used to play as a child. It's the same pool. It must be. But it's tiny. The "giant" rock (subject.he/she) used to jump off is about knee high. The "deep end" barely covers (subject.his/her) ankles. (subject.He/she) stands there in the water, trying to make sense of it.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) climbs up onto the giant rock, all the way to knee height, looks around to make sure nobody's watching, and jumps. It's a very short jump. It's also exactly as much fun as it used to be. (subject.He/she) does it four more times. (child), a child, appears on the bank and watches gravely. (subject) offers the rock. (child) accepts.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) sits on the edge and lets (subject.his/her) feet dangle in the water. The pool hasn't changed. (subject.He/she) has. It isn't sad, exactly. It's strange and a little funny, to have been so small once that this was an ocean. (subject.He/she) looks at (subject.his/her) big feet in the little pool and smiles. Then (subject.he/she) goes home, a bit taller than (subject.he/she) came.
